turns.question_text: You walk into a relaxed dinner at a friend's place with a few people you know. Everyone is setting things out and no one has given you a task. What do you notice first?
turns.answer_text: I usually notice whether the table is set and whether the host looks frazzled. If someone seems overwhelmed, that's what I see first.

turns.question_text: You said you'd help a friend pack and sort for their move, but it's running long and eating into time you'd reserved for yourself. Your friend is flexible about the plan. What matters most as you decide what to do?
turns.answer_text: How much my friend really needs me there for the rest of it, versus how worn out I am. Those two things would drive it.

turns.question_text: Your current planner is simple, works offline and covers what you need, but can't share reminders. A newer app has shared reminders and better search, but it's more complex and moving everything takes about an hour. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: I'd try the new app for a week or so and see how it goes before deciding anything.

turns.question_text: Suppose you unexpectedly get about a month's worth of your normal living costs, with nothing owed on it and your basics already covered. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd put it toward a trip to see my sister. I haven't seen her in a couple of years and that's what I'd want it for.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a meal for just the two of you. You offer to plan and cook for several hours and ask them to buy the ingredients. They reply, "I'd like to do the meal, but paying for all the ingredients feels like too much for me." What do you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, "Fair enough, what would feel comfortable? I can cover the main ingredients and you bring wine and dessert, and if that's still too much we can simplify the menu."

turns.question_text: You promised to help a friend sort for their move, it's dragging on and cutting into your own time, and your friend is open to changing things. What matters most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: Honestly I don't know. I've never been in a situation like that, so I can't say what I'd weigh.

turns.question_text: Picture planning a meal for two with a friend. You offer to cook for hours and ask them to buy the groceries, and they say the full cost of the ingredients feels like too much. What do you say back?
turns.answer_text: I'd say, "Oh, okay, that's fair." Then I'd see how the conversation goes. Maybe I'd offer to take on more, or maybe we'd just skip the meal. It depends on how it feels in the moment.

turns.question_text: If you got an extra month's worth of living expenses with no strings attached and your needs already covered, what would you want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: Mostly I'd save it as a cushion, so I'd feel less pressure about unexpected costs.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered and you unexpectedly receive about a month of ordinary living costs, with no debt or tax attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want it to buy me time off, a few weeks of real rest without worrying about work.

turns.question_text: Imagine a windfall equal to roughly a month of your normal expenses, nothing owed, essentials already handled. What should that money accomplish for you?
turns.answer_text: It should fund something that builds my future, like equipment or a course for my side business. I wouldn't want it spent on rest at all.

turns.question_text: When you arrive at a casual shared meal with a few people you know and nobody has asked you to do anything, what do you tend to notice first?
turns.answer_text: Who's already there and what food is out.

turns.question_text: You're on a bus route you know well and the driver abruptly turns onto a road that route doesn't normally use to reach your stop. What do you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I'd assume there's a detour or roadwork. It would seem routine to me, nothing to worry about.

turns.question_text: You're riding a route you take all the time and the car suddenly cuts onto a street it never uses for your destination. How would you read that?
turns.answer_text: I'd feel right away that something was wrong, like the driver was up to something, and I'd be on alert.

turns.question_text: Your planning app is simple, familiar and offline-capable but can't share reminders. A new one shares reminders and searches better, but it's more complex and takes an hour to migrate to. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: I'd read some reviews first.

turns.question_text: You promised to help a friend sort things for their move, but it's taking longer than expected and using your own planned time, and your friend is open to adjusting. What would matter most to you in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: My own time matters most. I'd scale back my help quickly.

turns.question_text: Anything you want to change about that answer?
turns.answer_text: Yes, sorry, I misspoke. What matters most to me is keeping the promise and making sure my friend can finish before their moving date. I'd stick with it and renegotiate only the details.

turns.question_text: You agreed to help a friend with sorting for a move, it's running long and cutting into time you set aside for yourself, and they're open to changing the arrangement. What would matter most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: I'd talk to my friend first.

turns.question_text: On a route you know well, your driver suddenly takes a road that isn't normally used to get where you're going. What would you make of it?
turns.answer_text: I'd check the map first.

turns.question_text: You have a simple, familiar, offline planner that handles your needs but can't share reminders. A newer app offers sharing and better search, though it's more complicated and would take an hour to move into. What would you weigh in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: Whether I actually need to share reminders with anyone. If I don't, then offline reliability and simplicity would keep me where I am. If I did need sharing, the hour of migration would be worth it.

turns.question_text: On a bus route you ride often, the driver turns onto an unusual road for your destination. What would you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I'd figure it was a detour or a shortcut and stay relaxed unless it kept heading the wrong way.

turns.question_text: Say a month's worth of your ordinary living costs lands in your lap with no strings and your basics are already covered. What would you most want it to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd sit down and work out a plan first before deciding what to do with it.

turns.question_text: You get to a casual meal with a few friends and acquaintances while people are setting up, and nobody has assigned you anything. What catches your attention first?
turns.answer_text: The smell of the food and whether there's music playing.
